items.q: Design a pipeline ingesting fundamentals from 50 sources daily, serving batch analytics and a near-real-time dashboard.
items.a: Three layers: (1) Ingestion -- NiFi fetches data and lands raw files in S3, config-driven per source. (2) Processing -- Spark validates types and business rules; invalid records go to dead-letter S3 with alerts; valid records become Parquet partitioned by date. (3) Serving -- Spark batch jobs query processed data for full analytics; pre-aggregated daily rollups feed the dashboard so it does not hit the heavy pipeline on every page load.

items.q: How do you design so adding source 51 doesn't require a code change?
items.a: Config-driven: store per-source metadata in a config table (DynamoDB or S3 JSON) -- URL, auth, format, schema, validation rules, schedule. The ingestion code reads this at runtime and operates generically. Adding source 51 is adding a config row. Zero code changes, zero deploy.

items.q: What is idempotency and why is it essential?
items.a: An idempotent pipeline produces the same result regardless of how many times it runs on the same input. Re-running today's pipeline should not duplicate records. Implement via mode('overwrite') on Parquet partitions, MERGE statements in SQL, date-partitioned output paths. Enables safe reruns -- how you fix bugs without corrupting data.

items.q: A Spark job that ran fine for 6 months suddenly takes 10x longer. Walk through your investigation.
items.a: Check data first: did input volume change? Did a new skewed key appear? Did a source send malformed records causing type coercion? Only after ruling out data: did a recent deploy change the query? In Spark UI: which stage got slow, is one task an outlier (skew), did a new Exchange appear in the plan?

items.q: You discover a bug corrupting 2% of records for 3 months. What order do you act in?
items.a: (1) Deploy the fix to stop further corruption. (2) Scope the blast radius -- which records, sources, time period, downstream consumers. (3) Communicate proactively before being asked. (4) Plan and execute backfill. Don't do all at once -- stop the bleeding, understand scope, communicate, fix history, in that order.

items.q: Tell me about a time you disagreed with a technical decision.
items.a: Template: describe the decision and why you disagreed. How you raised it -- specific reasoning or a small prototype, not just opinion. Result: even if overruled, you supported the team decision and ideally something from your concern was addressed. Interviewers want professional disagreement AND commitment afterward.

items.q: How would you push back on an unrealistic deadline?
items.a: Lead with trade-offs not refusal: we can hit that date if we scope to X, or hit full scope two weeks later. Give the decision-maker a real choice. Back it with a breakdown of remaining work. Accept they might still choose the original deadline -- your job is ensuring they decide with full information.

items.q: What does code review mean to you?
items.a: Beyond syntax: correctness under edge cases, testability, security/performance risks (non-parameterized query, .collect() on a large DataFrame), intent clarity for someone reading cold in 6 months. Also: specific positive feedback so people understand what good looks like, not just what's wrong.

items.q: How would you version a dataset schema without breaking existing consumers?
items.a: Additive (new nullable columns): Parquet handles automatically -- existing readers see null. Breaking changes: new versioned path (v2/) that new consumers opt into while old consumers stay on v1, or a transition period where both field names coexist before deprecating the old one on a communicated timeline. Never break consumers without a migration path.

items.q: How do you test transformation logic without running the full dataset?
items.a: Create a representative test dataset: 10-20 rows covering edge cases (nulls, duplicates, boundary values). Write unit tests: given this input, assert this output. pytest + assert_frame_equal for pandas; local SparkSession for PySpark. Test the function in isolation -- integration tests on full pipelines live separately as slower tests.

items.q: Walk me through your capstone project end-to-end.
items.a: Template using your real capstone: Source -> Python extraction (pandas+pyodbc) -> S3 raw -> EMR Spark validates and transforms -> Parquet partitioned by date -> Grafana dashboard (records, duration, errors). Idempotent via mode('overwrite'). State one honest thing you'd change -- for example, shuffle partitions set too high for the data volume.

items.q: What is your 90-day plan as Lead I?
items.a: Day 1-30: understand before changing -- read all code, run every job, interview the team, review 6 months of incidents. Day 31-60: deliver the highest-value lowest-risk improvement to build credibility. Day 61-90: propose the medium-term architectural improvement as a written document with trade-offs, lead the discussion, begin execution.
